question: Which of the following rebellions was led by traditional land soldiers (foot soldiers) in Odisha?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Paika Rebellion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Paika Rebellion** of 1817, also known as the **Paika Bidroha**, was led by the **Paikas**, the traditional militia or foot soldiers of Odisha.
 
• The rebellion was primarily against the oppressive policies of the **British East India Company**, including heavy taxation and the loss of land rights by the Paikas.
 
• The leader of this rebellion was **Bakshi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar**, a prominent military commander of the Khurda Kingdom who played a significant role in organizing the revolt.
 
• Paikas served as **land-owning militia** under the Gajapati kings of Odisha and provided military service in return for land grants. However, the British confiscated their lands, leading to widespread discontent.
 
• The rebellion is considered one of the first organized uprisings against British colonial rule in India, occurring much before the **First War of Indian Independence in 1857**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of the Paika Rebellion:**

 
 
• The Paikas were a hereditary warrior class who also acted as peasant militia during peacetime.
 
• With the advent of British rule, their land tenure system was disrupted, and they were heavily taxed, pushing them into poverty.
 
• The British confiscated the lands of many Paikas under the **Permanent Settlement System**, leaving them landless and stripping them of their traditional warrior status.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Rebellion:**
 
 
• The rebellion started in **March 1817** and quickly spread across various parts of Odisha, including Khurda, Puri, and Cuttack.
 
• The Paikas attacked British officials, looted treasury offices, and burnt police stations.
 
• Although the rebellion was eventually suppressed, it inspired later movements against British rule in Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Paika Rebellion:**
 
 
• The rebellion holds a significant place in Indian history as one of the earliest revolts against British colonial oppression.
 
• In 2017, the Government of India recognized the Paika Rebellion as the first war of Indian independence and commemorated its 200th anniversary.
 
 
 
• **Other Revolts for Comparison:**
 
 
• **Ahom Revolt:** A revolt in Assam against British annexation in the early 19th century, led by the Ahom nobility.
 
• **Wahabi Movement:** An Islamic reformist movement in India during the 19th century, aimed at purifying Islam and resisting colonial rule.
 
• **Faraizi Revolt:** A religious movement in Bengal during the 19th century that later evolved into an anti-British struggle under the leadership of Haji Shariatullah and his son Dudu Miyan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Paika Rebellion** was not a spontaneous uprising but a well-organized movement that involved different sections of society, including zamindars, tribal leaders, and peasants.
